entries.reason: A shared inference substrate for existing policies: adapters, KV reuse, fused kernels, graph replay and parallel services preserve model semantics. This is reusable deployment infrastructure rather than a new control model.
A portable C++ runtime with input/output adapters, model-head plugins and reusable execution kernels. It hosts multiple VLA/WAM architectures without defining a new learned policy.

AFM is a distinct future-memory consumer that compresses RGB/tactile foresight into slots for an existing ACT actor. Its reusable contribution is the representation-to-action interface, not a learned world model.

Modality Subspace Activation is a weight-preserving hidden-state intervention built from SVD anchor subspaces and applied before the existing language head. It is a reusable inference method, with sensitivity/accuracy tradeoffs.

The action-conditioned egocentric video generator is used to resimulate demonstrations for a separately initialized downstream robot model. Its memory and geometric action-conditioning mechanisms belong to a reusable prediction backbone.

The main contribution supplies a causal camera-generation backbone and rendering service to external physics/policy systems. Its separately post-trained trajectory-policy variant does not erase the reusable simulator-backbone role.
AFP predicts task-relevance masks and transfers their grounding into existing policies through auxiliary attention supervision. The standalone perception module is removed from deployed control.

A reusable adaptation recipe learns noise-selection policies for frozen generative controllers from inverted human corrections. It applies across host architectures rather than introducing one new WAM.
A video foundation backbone learns camera-aware multiview dynamics and reusable geometry-related features while receiving actions externally. No action head or complete robot policy is specified.

A host-independent training loss multiplier reweights demonstrated action timesteps by motion. It changes neither deployment architecture nor control interface and is reusable across action regression and generative policies.

KeyStone is a training-free sampling/selection wrapper for existing stochastic policies: shared context, parallel samples and medoid-based selection. It introduces no learned world model or full planning system.

STAR/JDMD provide a camera-controlled autoregressive video generator with cached reference/history and geometric conditioning. The learned output is reusable visual simulation rather than selected robot actions.

PersistWorld is a post-training method for an existing Ctrl-World backbone, using shared-prefix rollouts, relative rewards and contrastive denoising. Its central reusable contribution is stabilizing model training.

X-World supplies an action-conditioned multiview video backbone behind an external driving policy, with separate control adapters and causal streaming. The predictor is reusable without inheriting a complete control algorithm.

The core contribution is reusable dense image/video embeddings learned by self-supervised prediction. Manipulation and navigation add separate dynamics models and search, making the pretrained encoder a clear component.

Ctrl-World is a separately trained action-conditioned visual simulator consumed by existing policies for evaluation and synthetic-data collection. Its predictive interface is reusable; it does not itself choose actions.

DINOv3 explicitly provides pretrained global and dense visual descriptors for downstream heads. Its representation-learning and distillation mechanisms are reusable WAM perception components, without action outputs.

DreamDojo pretrains and adapts an action-conditioned video simulator; external policy and value models perform action selection. Its reusable prediction backbone and proxy-action interface support component placement.

HiLAM learns variable-duration latent skills and aligned supervision for separately fine-tuned hierarchical policies. The transferable latent-action/skill representation is the reusable contribution, not a deployed world-model planner.

A consistency-based visual dynamics model exposes a learned observation simulator to separate humans or imitation policies. Encoder, decoder and action-conditioned predictor form a reusable policy-training/evaluation backbone.

The study learns constrained latent actions and predictive representations from natural videos, then fits separate real-action interfaces. The reusable representation/pretraining mechanism is distinct from the downstream CEM planning evaluation.

MIND-V decomposes instructions and generates affordance- and trajectory-conditioned visual subgoals. A separate OpenVLA-OFT policy receives auxiliary visual supervision; the video generator does not itself output motor actions. Classify the reusable hierarchical visual world model, without turning its downstream policy experiment into a unified action model.

AINA predicts future fingertip trajectories from object and fingertip observations, then a separate inverse-kinematics controller converts them into joint commands. Its reusable contribution is an imitation policy and embodied action representation, without learned future-world dynamics.

PAN combines an autoregressive state-token predictor with a video renderer to simulate language-specified interactions. Actions are supplied conditions and planning uses an external VLM; this is an interactive prediction backbone, not an executable motor-action head.

Cosmos Predict2.5/Transfer2.5 provide controllable video and action-conditioned prediction backbones. Robot-policy augmentation and inverse-model pseudo-labeling use separate downstream policies, so these applications do not establish a joint executable-action predictor.

LongScape routes context to specialized CogVideoX video-generation experts. Robot action annotations partition training segments, while inference routes from text and visual context and produces video; no executed action policy is specified.

LAWM learns latent action chunks with an auxiliary world-model objective, then removes the world model before supervised robot adaptation and deployment. Its transferable contribution is an action representation and pretraining interface rather than a deployed predictive-control system.

MoVieDrive jointly denoises RGB, depth and semantic video under supplied layouts and camera conditions. These are reusable scene-generation modalities; the report explicitly leaves closed-loop driving simulation as future work and documents no action head.

Seedance 1.0 is a text/image-conditioned video-generation family with visual compression, denoising, prompt rewriting and refinement. The described inference pipeline produces videos rather than selecting or executing robot actions.

GAIA-2 generates multi-view driving video conditioned on supplied speed, curvature and other control variables. Its controllability is a predictive/simulation interface; it does not itself select the vehicle actions in a feedback controller.

Wan supplies a causal video autoencoder and diffusion-transformer family for video generation, conditioning and editing. The report describes visual denoising and multiple generation interfaces without an executable-action or planning module.

Gemma 3 combines a language decoder with SigLIP-based visual input and supports text, image and video-understanding tasks. Its reusable contribution is a language/vision-language backbone, not world-state forecasting or action generation.

Cosmos-Transfer1 adds multimodal ControlNet-style conditioning to a frozen generative video model. Its robot and driving uses concern synthetic visual data and externally supplied controls, with downstream planners or policies remaining separate.

FAST is a reusable action tokenizer: normalize continuous action chunks, apply a DCT, quantize and use byte-pair encoding for VLA prediction. It neither learns future-world dynamics nor supplies a complete model-based control algorithm.

CogVideoX develops a spatiotemporal video VAE and expert-transformer denoiser for text/image-conditioned video generation. Shared attention and joint frame generation provide a reusable visual backbone, not an executable action predictor.

Diffusion Policy represents a visuomotor action distribution with conditional denoising and executes action chunks in a receding-horizon loop. It is a reusable policy class; the report specifies no learned future-state rollout or world-model planner.

DriveDreamer-2 converts language-defined traffic scenarios into trajectories/maps and multi-view driving videos. Its experiments use generated data for perception, without a learned online driving controller; the reusable contribution is conditional scene generation.

EgoBridge supplies domain-alignment and imitation-training machinery using paired human/robot sequences, dynamic-time-warping structure and optimal transport. The deployed policy maps observations to actions without a learned predictive world rollout, so the reusable transfer-training method belongs with components.

FAST-LIVO2 estimates current state and maps through LiDAR, IMU and direct visual updates. Its downstream UAV planning/MPC is separate; the contribution is a reusable odometry and spatial-estimation subsystem rather than learned world-action generation.

LAPA learns discrete latent actions from frame pairs and uses them to pretrain a policy before labeled robot-action adaptation. Imagined visual decoding is separate from deployed policy inference, making the reusable latent-action representation/pretraining interface the appropriate component.

MeanFlow introduces an average-velocity generative formulation and training identity enabling one-step image synthesis. This general generative-model mechanism is reusable independently of any robot policy or predictive-control loop.

Mixture-of-Transformers supplies modality-specific transformer computation with shared attention for multimodal foundation models. Its language/image/speech and Transfusion experiments concern reusable backbone architecture, not robot actions or future-state control.

HIL-SERL integrates human interventions, demonstration-assisted model-free actor-critic learning, learned rewards and low-level controllers. It is a reusable robot-policy training framework without an explicit future-world predictor; this differs from the complete model-based RL systems retained in foundational work.

RLVR-World is a reinforcement-learning post-training method for existing world predictors, using verifiable future-state rewards. Actions remain supplied conditions and downstream control/planning systems are separate, so the portable optimization method is the component.
PaliGemma combines SigLIP and Gemma for transferable image-conditioned language and structured perception. It provides a VLM backbone rather than a world dynamics model or executable policy.

DINOv2 trains reusable image and patch representations with self-distillation and masked-feature objectives, then evaluates frozen features with downstream probes. Video action recognition predicts labels rather than executable actions; its contribution is the visual representation.

GenAD pretrains a general driving-video predictor and explores action-conditioned prediction and a separate planning adapter. The report describes future trajectories as supplied conditions and a planner reading frozen visual features, not a single generator that directly executes control; the reusable predictive backbone is the principal component.

Genie learns a tokenizer, latent-action model and action-conditioned dynamics to generate interactive visual environments. The separate CoinRun imitation/calibration experiment does not turn the simulator into a complete model-based RL controller; the reusable world-simulation backbone is the primary contribution.

DMD2 improves diffusion-model distillation with a learned fake-score critic, adversarial training and few-step student procedures. It transfers image-generator behavior rather than learning a world/action interface or complete robot controller.

Generalized Knowledge Distillation trains language-model students on their own generated prefixes using teacher distributional feedback. It is a reusable distillation objective/procedure, without a physical world model or action-execution interface.

DMD distills a pretrained diffusion image model into a fast generator using real/fake score differences and an auxiliary regression term. Its reusable contribution is the teacher-to-student training mechanism, not action-conditioned dynamics or control.

Prismatic VLMs studies and implements vision encoders, projectors and language backbones for image-conditioned text and coordinate prediction. Feature fusion and training recipes support a reusable VLM family; no dynamics rollout, action extraction or execution is evaluated.

This empirical model-free SAC study supplies reward, termination, reset-accounting and timeout-selection methods for learning goal-reaching policies. It contains no learned dynamics or imagined planner; its reusable contribution is the policy-training formulation and exploration setup rather than foundational world-model theory.

SERL packages demonstration-assisted model-free RL, reward/reset learning and compliant robot control into a reusable training software suite. Actor actions and reset policies are learned without future-state prediction, distinguishing it from the full model-based RL systems retained here.

The Sora overview describes a latent-patch video compression and diffusion-transformer generator. Qualitative world consistency and a Minecraft basic-policy claim lack a specified executed-action interface, so the supported contribution is a generative video backbone rather than a complete world-action controller.

Stable Video Diffusion develops reusable video pretraining, latent denoising and conditioning for text-to-video, image-to-video and novel-view synthesis. Camera conditions govern generated imagery; no executable action policy or feedback planning loop is supplied.
A reusable action-conditioned driving-video predictor and diffusion renderer; supplied controls shape imagery, while no learned controller or policy-learning loop is established.
The vision encoder, adapter and language decoder provide reusable image understanding and grounding through text and box outputs.
A pretrained causal language backbone for text prediction and prompting, rather than a control system or planning theory.
Explicit Gaussian scene representation and differentiable rasterization supply a reusable static-scene rendering component; neither temporal dynamics nor action selection is learned.
Consistency endpoint maps are reusable image-generation primitives, trained by distillation or directly from data; their sampling role fits generative components.
This DINO is the DETR object detector, not the self-supervised DINO encoder. Its image features, anchor queries and box/class predictions form a reusable visual-perception module.
Rectified-flow velocity regression, reflow and endpoint distillation supply reusable generative transport machinery without a control loop.

PaLM-E is a reusable sensor-conditioned language backbone producing answers and high-level skill text; separate controllers execute its outputs. Its planning use does not make the paper primarily a planning-theory work.
DiT is a transformer denoising backbone for image latents, with reusable conditioning blocks rather than an environment-control system.
SigLIP learns aligned image/text embeddings and pairwise compatibility scores; the reusable representation objective and encoders are components.
Latent diffusion combines perceptual compression with conditional denoising as reusable image-generation machinery; the existing report does not establish video dynamics or action control.
Low-rank weight updates and mergeable adaptation are reusable training/inference techniques, independent of a particular world model or controller.
Camera-to-BEV lifting and 3D detection provide a reusable spatial perception module for current scenes, without learned action-conditioned future prediction or control.
CLIP supplies reusable aligned image/text encoders and prompt-defined visual classification. These embeddings provide visual representations for downstream models.
T5 provides a reusable pretrained text-to-text encoder-decoder and transfer recipe; its unified task interface produces text, not a complete world-model control system.
GPT-3 is a reusable autoregressive language backbone evaluated through fixed-weight prompting and continuation, rather than a planning or control framework.
Preference reward modeling and KL-constrained PPO form a reusable alignment procedure for text generation; the method neither models environmental transitions nor supplies a classic MBRL system.

DIAYN learns reusable skill-conditioned feedback policies and a discriminator, then demonstrates their reuse for initialization, hierarchical composition and imitation. It does not contain a learned world model.

The concrete multi-sensor odometry estimator supplies reusable state and calibration estimates. This is a perception module, rather than a general treatment of probabilistic estimation or a control planner.
Dynamics randomization and recurrent adaptation supply a transferable sim-to-real training technique. The policy is trained in an external simulator rather than a learned-model RL loop.
Pairwise feedback trains a reusable reward predictor that supervises policy learning. Its general preference-based training mechanism fits components; it does not learn a world transition model.

VQ-VAE’s encoder, discrete codebook, straight-through training and separately fitted prior are reusable tokenization/generation components; supplied actions in its video experiment are not inferred policies.
PointNet is a reusable permutation-invariant point-set encoder and 3D recognition/segmentation architecture, without a planning or world-model learning loop.

AEVB provides the reusable variational autoencoder and differentiable latent-sampling training mechanism. Its concrete encoder/generator role fits generative components despite the underlying variational derivation.
